title: Docs: Route-level A/B testing (Console) — concepts, setup, metrics, troubleshooting
author: Wei Chen
description: Summary: Adds the first public documentation set for Route-level A/B testing in Console (beta). Covers core concepts (route-scoped experiments, variants, deterministic assignment/stickiness), step-by-step setup in Console, what metrics are collected and how to interpret them (latency/TTFT, cost attribution, error rates, exposure counts), operational guardrails + rollback behavior, and a troubleshooting guide based on early beta feedback (variant flipping, results mismatch vs customer dashboards, 429 spikes due to capacity constraints, and why some fields are intentionally not exposed for privacy/cardinality). Scope: Hosted + Dedicated (Private called out as follow-on / availability varies). Notes: Aligns terminology with Console UI copy ("Control"/"Variant", "Start", "Stop", "Rollback") and references the standardized experiment telemetry schema without publishing internal event payloads. This is intentionally written as beta docs and includes limitations (no bandits, limited exports, quality eval attachment is "optional" and may be gated).
body:
## What
This PR adds a new public docs section for **Route-level A/B testing** in the Redwood Console. The goal is to provide customers enough context to safely run experiments on production traffic for a specific API route (ex: `/v1/chat/completions`), understand what metrics Redwood collects by default, and troubleshoot common misconfigurations.

## Why
We have beta design partners onboarding now and Support is seeing early confusion around (a) deterministic assignment and "variant flipping", (b) why experiment results can differ from customer-side dashboards, and (c) safe rollback / guardrail behavior. The docs in this PR should reduce support load and make experiments safer to run.

## Audience
- Engineers / ML engineers running inference in production
- Platform teams who own routing, SLOs, and cost controls

## Docs added/updated
- New: `docs/console/experiments/route-level-ab-testing.md`
  - Concepts: route scope, variants, allocations, eligibility, scheduling
  - Deterministic assignment + stickiness: what it means and what inputs are used at a high level (no raw PII)
  - Interaction with rollouts/fallback routing (high-level precedence explanation, links to rollouts docs)
- New: `docs/console/experiments/route-level-ab-testing-setup.md`
  - Console flow: create → validate → start → monitor → stop/rollback
  - Recommended starting splits (90/10) and ramp guidance
  - Naming guidance ("control" semantics, stable identifiers for variants)
- New: `docs/console/experiments/route-level-ab-testing-metrics.md`
  - Metrics glossary: p50/p95/p99 latency, TTFT, token counts, error/timeout rate, exposure counts
  - Cost attribution: what is and isn’t included, and how to compare variants fairly
  - Interpreting low-volume experiments + confidence indicators (beta)
- New: `docs/console/experiments/route-level-ab-testing-guardrails.md`
  - Guardrail examples (latency regression, error rate thresholds)
  - What happens on guardrail breach (alerts + rollback workflow, depending on policy)
  - Operational checklist before starting an experiment
- New: `docs/console/experiments/route-level-ab-testing-troubleshooting.md`
  - Variant assignment is not stable (missing/unstable client identifier; retries/stream reconnect behavior)
  - Console vs customer dashboards don’t match (windowing, sampling, region filters, metric definitions)
  - Elevated 429s / throttling after starting experiment (capacity constraints; reduce split, switch region/tier, use rollback)
  - Why you can’t add arbitrary high-cardinality tags
- Updated: `docs/console/experiments/index.md` (adds nav entries)
- Updated: `docs/console/rollouts/overview.md` (adds a short cross-link + definitions section)

## Notable content decisions
- Privacy: Docs explicitly state that assignment is deterministic and privacy-safe; avoids listing exact hashing keys or logging payload fields.
- Cardinality: Added a dedicated callout explaining why we limit dimensions in experiment breakdowns (protects performance/cost and keeps dashboards usable).
- Beta limitations: Calls out that exports/reporting APIs may be limited in beta, and availability may differ by deployment mode/tier.

## Screenshots
- Placeholder callouts added for Console screenshots; will replace with final captures once DES-142 copy is locked.

## Validation
- Local docs build: `pnpm lint && pnpm build`
- Link check: `pnpm check-links`

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)
- Add a short ‘quickstart’ snippet with example API route naming conventions for multi-tenant apps.
- Add a support-facing appendix on incident response that deep-links to the public-facing rollback page.

Refs: PM-481, SUP-3928, SUP-3921
commits: docs(console): add route-level A/B testing overview + setup guide
docs(console): add metrics glossary and cost attribution notes for experiments
docs(nav): wire new experiment pages into Console docs index
docs(copy): align terminology with Console UI (control/variant, start/stop/rollback)
conversation: Elliot Price (review): Please add an explicit note that exposure counts can be sampled in some cases, so customers don’t try to reconcile 1:1 with request logs.
Wei Chen (author): Added a note in the Metrics page under Exposure volume + added a troubleshooting bullet about sampling vs exact counts.
Paula Mendes (review): The cost section should clarify that comparisons are best done with the same prompt distribution and the same max_tokens. Also mention TTFT separately from end-to-end latency.
Wei Chen (author): Updated metrics glossary: added TTFT definition + emphasized prompt/parameters consistency for cost comparisons.

Sean Gallagher (review): Guardrails page: please add a pre-flight checklist (alerts configured, rollback permissions, on-call aware) and link to rollback steps. Also make sure we warn about 429s when shifting to constrained capacity.
Wei Chen (author): Added pre-flight checklist + explicit 429/capacity note, and linked to rollback section.

Tessa Morgan (review): Copy: prefer “variant” over “treatment” throughout; also “Stop experiment” vs “Pause” to match the UI. Can we add a short definition of “Control” so it doesn’t read as implying ‘best’?
Wei Chen (author): Updated terminology and added a short definition: Control = baseline config you are comparing against (not necessarily best).
Marissa Cole (approval): Looks good for beta. Please ensure the first paragraph calls out route scope and that experiments can compare model variants OR config changes.
Wei Chen (author): Updated opening paragraph + added examples (model swap, quantization profile, decoding params).
Logan Wright (approval): +1 after sampling and cardinality notes. Thanks for keeping payload details abstract.
release_notes: Public docs (beta): Added Route-level A/B testing documentation (concepts, setup, metrics, guardrails, troubleshooting) with Console navigation links.
